summary: Inflight queue saturation during EU peak causing degraded streaming and 5xx spike for Quantumiq
description:
Issue summary:
During the EU morning peak on 2026-03-10 (~07:12-08:05 UTC), Quantumiq experienced degraded streaming responses and an elevated 5xx rate (~12% 5xx on customer route) caused by sustained inflight request queue saturation. A sharp increase in long-context generation requests (avg seq length ~8k tokens per request) from a single customer key triggered retry amplification and queue buildup in the local reservoir queue.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: intermittent streaming silence, truncated chunks, and increased 5xx/502 responses for ~53 minutes.
- Business: Quantumiq reported product disruptions for internal demos in EU region; support escalation to CS and Sales.
- Billing exposure: tracked as potential overbilling for replays and retries; credit pending.

Timeline (high level):
- 07:12 UTC: Spike detected via route-level SLO alert (p50/p95 token latency increase + 5xx surge).
- 07:17 UTC: Automated graceful-degradation policy attempted fallback to quantized variant but observed backlog amplification.
- 07:25 UTC: Autoscaler did not provide immediate relief due to GPU slot starvation and quota caps on the dedicated pool.
- 07:30-08:05 UTC: SRE engaged; applied temporary per-key concurrency cap and disabled fallback routing for the affected prefix.
- 08:05 UTC: 5xx rate returned to baseline and streaming resumed; remediation actions rolled forward.

Steps to reproduce (repro recipe for engineering):
1) Issue a sustained burst of long-context generation requests (prompt + 8k tokens target) with client-side 3xx retry policy, concurrency ~120 per key, to the Quantumiq route in eu-west.
2) Observe sustained growth of inflight reservoir queue and KV cache thrashing leading to repeated request cancellation and 502 responses.
3) Reproduces when per-customer concurrency caps are higher than pool allowance and autoscaler backoff windows align with the burst.

Relevant logs & links:
- Route dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/routes/quantumiq-eu/overview
- Trace sample: span IDs: trace-77a3.., trace-77a4.. (attached in telemetry bundle)
- Slack escalation: #support-quantumiq (thread TS03K9J4Q)

investigation_notes: Measured queue growth: reservoir inflight queue for the Quantumiq route grew from baseline ~20 to >110 concurrent inflight requests during peak (sustained for ~18 minutes).

Autoscaler behavior: GPU pool autoscaler did add nodes but new nodes became usable only after scheduler slot warmup (~6 minutes) due to container cold-start and model warmup time (KV cache population).
Retry amplification: client-side retry policy (3 retries with jitter) caused effective request fanout; combined with long per-request tokenization time this amplified inflight count.

Fallback routing side-effect: graceful fallback to quantized variant attempted to reduce latency but routed additional requests into a smaller reserved pool, causing a local hotspot and backpressure loop.
Telemetry gap: exact trace for earliest 07:12-07:17 window is partial due to sampling; full telemetry captured starting 07:18 when sampling rate was increased.
resolution: Immediate mitigation: applied per-key concurrency cap for Quantumiq (50) and disabled graceful fallback routing for the route. SRE drained the reservoir queue via a sliding drain script and temporarily increased pool capacity. Medium-term: merged PR to add early-reject policy for requests with sequence length >7k tokens when router-level concurrency exceeds threshold (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891).
